title: "Candidate Facebook"
body:
We need a singular source that holds a directory of EVERY individual who runs for public office. 

It needs to have a photo, a bio, a clear & concise position on a set list of topics (personally written & signed by the candidate), a list of all campaign contributions received by the candidate, and the candidate's voting record. This should be required as part of the filing process to run for office in the state.

It should also permit similarly "civil" communications where citizens can post concerns & ask questions of their representative.

title: Child‑Support Modernization / Administrative Reform
body: SC’s Family Court backlog is among the longest in the country because judges handle every issue, including routine child‑support math. SC needs more judges based on population, magistrates or clerks for routine matters, and automated recalculation to reduce delays and keep cases moving.

title: Honor the Radical Republicans of the Reconstruction period that stood their ground against conservatives
body:
South Carolina’s Constitutional Convention of 1868 is one of the most progressive in the history of our state. It established the public school system, affirmed that all 21+ year old males could vote regardless of if they owned property, and made divorce legal. It also nullified Black Codes.

When conservatives got back into power in 1890s, they happily took credit for the populist measures introduced by the Radical Republicans while re-establishing Black Codes.

It is past time for all Carolinians to learn about these brave reconstruction politicians.

body: I'm very concerned that South Carolina in general and Upstate in particular are overdeveloping natural woodlands. I live at in Fort Mill and I'm so disgusted that so many trees have been cut down to make way for apartments, houses, shopping centers, etc. I've watched hundreds of trees be chopped down everywhere. Noise has increased tenfold with nothing to muffle or block sounds from traffic mainly. You can here the traffic on 77 from almost everywhere in town. It wasn't like this even three years ago. There needs to be a moratorium on building.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Education
body: Education is the root of all problems. Teachers must be accountable for progress of students if when the child becomes an adult they are to be able to truly understand issues, vote intelligently and hold politicians accountable. Prepare youth for good paying jobs. Incentivize teachers with appropriate pay and bonuses for outstanding student performance. Thus attracting dedicated educators. Eliminate bloated administration. Spend on kids not bureaucracy.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Rent control for land leases.
body:
South Carolina has quite a few 55+ mobile home communities. They were once an affordable option for the elderly on fixed incomes or the disabled. Since investment firms have come in and bought up many of these communities the land leases have skyrocketed. Land leases mean you own your home but lease the land it sits on, there are no current laws to cap how high they can go. Tenants are held hostage because they cannot afford to move their homes, nor can they sell them with such high leases attached. 

I live in such a community and we need HELP.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Polarization
body: See a need to build bridges across difference
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Encourage unions
body: Unions provide individual workers with negotiating power that improves the workplace, from paychecks to benefits to community health.  Unions offer a more balanced conversation between employers and employees-- both sides of modern business and government operations which, in SC, are unfairly tilted in one direction.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Stop Subsidizing Data Centers by Citizens
body:
Data centers are huge and mislead the uneducated into assuming they must employ hundreds of people. In reality, after the construction equipment demobilizes, only a few dozen employees are ever hired.

A single AI data center uses the electricity equivalent of >500,000 houses each year. Data centers still collect economic development incentives & citizens pay to have additional electricity capacity built.

Our politicians lap up contributions from big tech, giving them tax incentives and then try to shove another data center in our back yards.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Insurance Reform
body:
S.C. insurance rates continue to skyrocket. Hundreds of thousands of homeowners policies have more than doubled in under 5 years. Premiums are going up. Deductibles are going up. Coverages are going down. 

BCBS is the only healthcare option for self insured. Why is it that United, Aetna, etc. says they can not sell to a regular person anymore? We are now required by Obama care to have insurance, however we can only buy it from BCBS?

Insurance executives are being awarded with outsized bonuses and lawyers reap the benefits from lawsuits and settlements.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Homelessness
body:
* Having housing should be the right of all human Beings.
* states in conjunction with Federal sources must provide paces for all homeless people to eat, live and sleep. 
citirs and states need to play the central role in this effort.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Utility Costs
body:
Solar electricity is now the cheapest energy for residences and businesses. 

the state needs to facilitate the solarizing of

1) all new buildings

2) parking lots

3) existing residences with subsidies and Solar refs that are sold on the market for business to buy to meet requirements of buying a portion of the electricity from green sources.

4) permission for households to choose their sources for electricity.  In NJ I bought my electricity from Texas Windfarms.

title: Voter approve voter approved  redistricting
body:
Virginia is proposing a bill that would allow voters to agree to the redistricting done by the political party in power. Such a proposal in South Carolina would help alleviate the impossible current geramandering strategy that has removed the voters' voice from voting.

A committee to study the Virginia proposal and it's viability here would be a good start.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Healthcare is a Human Right
body:
Healthcare is a human right.  As a Healthcare Practitioner and working in Healthcare over 26 years now, I have seen our Healthcare system change some for good and majority of it worse. 

South Carolina needs a better a Healthcare system for all.

I want to save lives as a RRT and change lives for the better but our Healthcare is denied for thousands as it is for profit and we need a Healthcare payor for all that is regulated and would allow Everyone to have insurance and not have to go bankrupt from current Healthcare insurance companies costs.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Diversity, Equity or equality for legislation
body: We have a need for DEI in our state legislature.  We seem to have gone backwards on equality for our state representatives and state laws. Turning back the clock to past biased opinions of separation or Segregation or division of individuals is not just wrong but is hurtful to our progress and outcomes for our states future generations.  Especially the children we have being taught division and separation again. My concern is our state is not moving towards progress but instead trying to rewind backwards to morally known wrongs.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Culture War politics
body: If we had legislators that actually worked on issues instead of grandstanding on religious views we could move into the current century.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Hemp for Land contamination reform
body:
We can use HEMP in many forms to create ENVIRONMENTAL GREEN INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION while stopping SYSTEMATIC POISONING OF CITIZENS BY MAJOR CORPORATIONS & GOVERNMENT. 

Unbiased approach to HEALTHIER LIVING..
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Referendum Process
body: In most states, there is a citizen referendum process that allows groups of citizens to petition to place something on a public ballot for voters. South Carolina does not have this, and I feel it limits South Carolinians’ ability to have their voices heard. If the state passes something constituents do not like, citizens should have the opportunity to change it. The same applies when there is a lack of legislative action on issues affecting the state’s residents.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: The Foster Care System
body: In this state and across our nation the foster care system is a dysfunctional, underfunded, unorganized, heartbreaking and never talked about mess!!! These are traumatized children with no hope, no rights, no voice, no future and many with no forever families. How many more children will we allow to slip through the cracks, to go on to prison, homelessness, drugs and death before something changes? What does it take to even get this discussed in ANY political race or office. Time has run out, these kids need a miracle!!!
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Incentivize Community Involvement
body: The gov. and the community need to make a cooperative investment - both in time and money - to write a new future for South Carolina. In short, incentivize individuals & businesses to design & execute localized solutions within a 5 year timespan. Offer homeless people gift cards for cleaning up / keeping the community clean. Use SC government platforms as a marketing tool to solicit bids from local contractors to fix infrastructure - "sell" the advertising space and start a bidding war. I could go on - childcare, healthcare, culture, education...
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: State of Healthcare is Dismal in SC
body: South Carolina sits in the middle tier nationally, earning an overall C+ grade in a 2025 healthcare scorecard. The state struggles most with cost (graded D+), while quality and access land at C+ and C, respectively. 	23% of residents report healthcare costs as a major financial burden. 	30% skipped doctor‑recommended care in the past year because they couldn’t afford it. Our state has an affordability and access problem. This is a huge challenge that our candidates for Governor need to address. I want to help, but how do I do that?
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Public Health & Environmental Protection
body: South Carolina desperately needs to update existing laws & legal tools to better promote the protection of human health and the environment. Many federal environmental regulations are being repealed, which opens up an opportunity & increased need for the state of South Carolina to step in & prioritize the health of our residents over profits. Our landscape and relationship with the outdoors is both economically beneficial to the state and a core part of our identity—yet we sell it out to polluters & developers and foot the bill by giving them tax cuts.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Roads
body: We need a comprehensive program to fix existing roads while expanding road capacity in those high traffic areas.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Mis- and Disinformation
body: Mis- and disinformation campaigns polarize South Carolinians and warp objective reality. Public officials should be removed from office for intentionally and knowingly lying to the public. Social media & artificial intelligence corporations that platform misleading/false statements & images aimed at inciting outrage & fear, sowing division, and confusing the issue(s) should be regulated. When what people form their political stances on is based on intentionally false information, we spend more time debating what is true than coming up with solutions.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Let SC Citizens have a say in our Laws
body: South Carolinians are dependent on our Representatives to be our voice, yet many support their parties opinion tho’ polls show the majority oppose much of SC Legislation. When laws that impact our State are passed, we should have a vote yay or nay.  Many States Legislatures have recently changed their Congressional maps.  Only California’s map was overwhelmingly passed by the people for the people. We are operating safe and secure elections, let’s start using them to ask the people to make a choice for their own lives and beliefs.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Mobile Home Parks Lot rent fees
body: Big investment companies are buying up Mobile Home Parks in SC and other states due to no lease or lot fee regulation, allowing them to increase fees at 16% and change leases to month by month instead of yearly, so they can take advantage of senior citizens living on fixed incomes.  They are also offering to provide government forms for folk with low incomes (who qualify) so the government can pay for their fees.  A loss to both the mobile home owners and the government.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Eviction Court
body: I'm Dalphine McFadden Woodward. I moved to Greenville with my two sons for better opportunities. I worked two jobs, to provide for my children. Then, I got pneumonia, in the hospital, out of work, causing an evicted. We lived different places & while my son was away, I slept in my car, while getting on my feet. I was rebuilding, my mother needed to moved in b/c of health, then our new apartment was burned down.  Other cities in SC & throughout the US have Housing Courts to help with the issues of evictions, yet Greenville, SC lacks one.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Election Integrity
body:
“Who gets to make the call.” includes redistricting, voter identification and campaign financing. Get these solved and many of the other issues will diminish.  

Redistricting - algorithmic approach not gerrymandering; let the chips fall where they may but it will be be consistent.

Voter Identification - only citizens of the US and valid photo ID get to vote.

campaign financing - only registered voters can contribute and certainly no out of state contributions. WE get to fund not outside interests.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Utilities
body: Utilities cost
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: School Vouchers for Public Schools
body: We should not use state taxes to fund private schools that are allowed to discriminate on the basis of sex, religion, disability, education experience etc. Also, they receive these funds with no accountability. This is a money scheme for the wealthy to subsidize their child's education while selectively choosing who they want to attend private schools. This is wrong and will leave public schools with more challenging students because they must accept "ALL" students.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Voting
body: End gerrymandering. Create an independent commission of citizens to draw all districts for elective office.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Prison Reform/Judicial Reform
body:
We have far too many of our citizens incarcerated unjustly due to lack of proper council, prejudicical and misleading prosecutors, sheer laziness of the people who are supposed to be protecting our rights, overly aggressive sentences based on nothing but hearsay, among other issues that cause South Carolina families undue trauma and distress. 

We need to do a better job from all aspects. But, treating each person as innocent until proven guilty is a start.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Non Support for ICE in SC
body: Do not command local or state law enforcement to assist or tolerate ICE arresting SC citizens.  They are a modern day Gestapo group.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Women's Health
body: Why is our legislature passing laws about what Healthcare women can or cannot receive? Our state Legislature does not have a medical degree. What goes on in our underpants, our bedrooms, and our doctor offices is no business of our government.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Infrastructure
body: We continue to develop our land and build, but we never develop infrastructure to support any of it. Our roads have to be some of the worst in the country. We need to improve what we have here now in order to improve our lives and support the growth that currently feels unsustainable.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Maternal Mortality
body: South Carolina has the 8th worst maternal mortality rate in the nation. Over a dozen of our counties don't have an OBGYN, leaving a maternal healthcare desert. Practitioners are reluctant to work in our state because of the restrictive, poorly written laws that put their licenses in jeopardy. Standard, life-saving reproductive care for women is crumbling in our state and that's reckless.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Legalize Hemp instead of taking it away!
body: As a person who has worked in the hemp industry for the last 3 years, I can assure you that nothing is going to stop kids/teens from getting their hands on things they’re not supposed to. SC choosing to ban/heavily regulate hemp is going to force people to seek unsafe options from the street. Thousands of SC residents depend on these products to help them with sleep, pain, and addiction withdrawal symptoms! Stop infantilizing adults and taking away our options by using children as a shield for your terrible politics! Educate yourself!
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Casino
body: I would like access to a nearby casino. I have lived my whole in South Carolina and have followed "the rules". I have worked hard, sacrificed and saved money. I have never asked any state or local agency for anything. Now that I have retired I believe I have the right to spend that the money in a way I would like. I do not need state and local "leaders" being my moral police and telling me how to spend my money. I enjoy going to a casino and I would like one in state.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Crandle to Career
body: South Carolina must address education equity and workforce alignment, rural health access, and affordable housing. The state can reform school funding, expand career pathways, strengthen public health systems, and incentivize mixed income development. These issues are interconnected. Education fuels workforce growth, health drives economic stability, and housing affects mobility. Strategic policy choices can shape long term prosperity for families and communities.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Disabled Chronic Pain Patients Rights
body: Patients with severe acute and chronic pain used to be safely managed under individualized medical care. Today, due to fear-driven regulation and enforcement pressure, patients are routinely forced into untreated pain, involuntary tapers, and inadequate medical care, even including individuals with documented surgical histories, severe injuries, lifelong incurable conditions AND CANCER! We are treated as criminal suspects rather than medical patients bc we need opioids to live. We need laws to protect both the doctors and disabled immediately.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Priorities
body:
1) Education

2) Healthcare

3) Jobs

4) Community involvement coordination
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Fair freedoms for all and focus on real issues not just hot topics
body: I would like to see our elected officials prioritize the daily concerns of their constituents instead of their own personal and party agendas.  I'd like to see issues like raising the quality of education, health, infrastructure, and protecting voting rights be their focus and not issues that small but loud well funded minority groups push.  I'd like for women to have the same freedoms as men when making medical decisions and for the government to stay out of those decisions.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: CULTURAL ISSUES
body: Stop with the low hanging fruit trying to appeal to a rapidly diminishing base. Control of our own bodies by leaving politics out of it / letting professionals and recipients decide what's best for them.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Medical Cannabis
body: The use of medical cannabis would be very advantageous for chronically ill people.., people with seizures, children with major health issues, loss of appetite, severe pain, PTSD, anxiety, panic attacks, any medicinal purpose medical marijuana can be used it should be brought to the table and properly voted for this legislation
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Child support enforcement
body: There needs to be an ongoing program to collect court ordered child support. It is financially necessary for single parents and grandparents with custody.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Legislative Immunity
body:
The current system of legislative immunity must be curtailed. 

While it is understandable that a lawmaker could need to have a trial moved until after the legislative session ends, some lawmakers abuse this privilege.

Legislators should not be allowed to use this privilege indefinitely, session after session, year after year.

Often defendants hire a lawyer legislator on their legal team for the sole purpose of having the ability to delay having their case tried. Brilliant defense strategy, horrific victim treatment.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: No Senior Tax on Seniors making less than $250,000.
body: For those over 65 making less than $250,000 a year, no state or local tax on SS, cars, pensions or property tax on the one home they reside in.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Judicial Reform
body:
Currently the JMSC is comprised of our legislators, who are coincidentally attorneys. Our judges are appointed by the JMSC. 

Lawyer legislators should be prohibited from practicing in front of the judges they appoint. How can a judge be impartial when the lawyer in front of him holds the keys to his continued employment? 

In any other forum this would easily be seen as a conflict of interest.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Term limits for politicians
body: No more senators/representatives that stay forever,  and think more of making money and sucking up to the top income makers instead of looking after their own people suffering in South Carolina. 2 terms max for US Senators and 5 for US Representatives.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Free college and tech school
body: All our kids deserve the chance to go to college or tech school for free. It would keep our kids here, improve the work force and bring in better companies with a well trained workforce.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Tort Reform
body: SC tort laws are written to protect corporations, insurance companies, & to enrich attorneys. 30% of our legislators are attorneys & S.C. small  businesses, the entire trucking industry, & regular citizens are being strangled by the tort rules they pass allowing them to benefit from every lawsuit (reaping as much as 40% + expenses). Insurance companies are not required to rebate any premiums when costs fall below projections & they reap excessive profits each year. The  2025 “tort reform” shifted medical costs to tax payers and added more regulations.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Free quality Childcare
body: Other States are doing it.  Give all our kids a good start.  Let moms go to work outside the home if they want or go to school. Free quality daycare for all residents.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Healthcare for all
body: Free Healthcare for all. Noone should die because they can't afford Healthcare.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Public Education
body: SC is actively dismantling public education thru the unconstitutional use of public funds for private schools & by enabling unauthorized use of ~10% of voucher funds for homeschooling. Weakening our already weak public education system. Creates a shadow educ system w/no accountability, allows re-trenchment of segregation & discrimination based on race, gender, religious beliefs, sexual orientation & abilities.  Disproportionately benefits the wealthy. It also allows education that is often not fact or science-based.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Property Tax Reform
body:
Historically, a fief is when one pays a lord for use of a land (or property) grant.

Without property tax reform and elimination, South Carolinians will never outright own their property.

This is unjust for everyone, but especially for seniors. As the value of real estate rises, a senior who paid $30,000 for a property can easily now be expected to pay property taxes on a property valued at $300,000 or more.

Property tax should not be assessed on anything except for real estate & only at the time of sale and paid by the new buyer at the current value.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Ineffective Government Leadership
body: Legislators intentionally misuse the time they spend in session to misdirect and stall bills and conversations they want to avoid. We are a small state that has the ability to execute all necessary annual legislative actions in the currently allocated time frame. Yet instead of addressing our ongoing issues, every year our lawmakers choose to squander the time rehashing abortion when we already have the toughest law in the country.  This is just one example of how they stall and misdirect the debate on new issues.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Election Reform
body:
Many of the issues posted reflect symptoms of systemic problems. "Politics is the allocation of resources."  The current election system is a systemic issue causing symptomatic problems like poor infrastructure. Unless we change the way our politicians are elected, we'll get the same political outcomes:

Poor infrastructure

Poor public education system

Poor Health Care system

which leads to poor opportunity, poor wages

The challenge for the Forum will to be to determine do we try to take on systemic issues or fix a symptom.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Housing, Public Transportation and affordability
body:
American Dream,  the promise that families can build a stable life, own a home is slipping out of reach for too many people

We have a chance to change that using public transportation strategy  leveraging federal infrastructure programs

* Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (IIJA)
* FTA Capital Investment Grants (CIG)
* FRA Corridor Identification & Development Program
* CRISI Rail Grants
These programs fund transit projects across US. For Upstate consider connecting key areas between Spartanburg to Clemson, supported by feeder systems like Greenville Connect.

title: Mental health
body: Find incentives for foster care parents.

title: Education Innovation
body: We need to get back to the basics when it comes to education. Publicly funded schools are enamored with the latest educational trends afraid that our students will be behind their peers. We need to be more focused on what kind of people we are forming than what skills students are learning. The skills we teach them today will be obsolete in just a few years. Part of this reform would involve being less obsessed with being able to scientifically measure every educational outcome. Testing success is paramount because of the attached funding.

title: Black history and its erasure

title: Decline in education
body: One of the biggest challenges in South Carolina is the continual decline of our education and low ranking compared to other states.

body: We need to ensure there is necessary infrastructure to accommodate all of the influx of new residents. It matters to me because the traffic in the Summerville area and between here and Charleston is horrendous at most times of the day.

title: Officials Slow to Act
body: We need to improve roadway infrastructure. I live in one of the fastest growing areas of the state and every single day there are roadway problems, yet local and state elected officials are slow to take action.

title: Daily Driving Challenges
body: We need to work together to fix roads, bridges, and infrastructure. It matters to me because I am driving every day.

title: Gas Tax Not Fixing Roads
body: We need to repair the roads. They raised the gas tax to fix the roads but, nothing seams to be happening. It matters to me because the taxes here are outrageous and the roads are still terrible.

title: Secondary Roads Falling Apart
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be repair all of the secandary roads across the state. They are all falling apart. This state doesn't even know how to repair the pot holes properly--yet our taxes keep going up every year!

title: Roads Playing Catch-Up
body: I want to solve infrastructure because every main road and feeder road needs to be addressed based on the volume of people moving to our state. Our roads are always playing catch up and we should be looking forward to addressing our 2050 needs. Every time I leave my house I am in traffic that is getting continuously worse.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Minutes Become Hours
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be infrastructure. It matters to me because roads and bridges are in poor condition, causing issues with tires and suspension. Insufficient capacity cause accidents and congestion. Trips that should be a few minutes have become an hour in the Charleston / Mount Pleasant and Hilton Head / Beaufort areas.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Overcrowded Services
body: Our infrastructure cannot meet the demand of the state's current growth. It affects us all! Our schools, roads, doctors offices, hospitals are over crowded. Our police and fire services are overwhelmed. The prices of houses for our children are unaffordable.  There has to be a better way!
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Commutes Taking Twice as Long
body: We need to fix the growing population and infrastructure. Traffic, failing roads and intersections make it hard to get around. I've lived here since 1998 and it takes a lot longer to get around than it did before. In some cases twice as long or more.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Infrastructure Affects Everything
body: I want us to tackle infrastructure. It matters to me because it affects daily life opportunity and the future of our communities.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Plan Roads for 2050
body: We need to improve infrastructure by 2050.  The state should start now by adding main roads, feeder roads and widening existing roads. Traffic is horrible. I live in the country and traffic has found us. It affects all of our travel plans, even just going to the grocery store. To stay out of the worst of traffic, we try and drive between 9am and 3pm.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Hour to Cross Town
body: I want us to tackle infrastructure. It matters to me because it often takes an hour to get across town due to traffic.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Need Passenger Rail
body: We need to do something about our state's infrastructure. The rest of the country and world are investing in public transit like high speed rail and we're adding a badly planned bus to Charleston that is only going to make traffic worse--why? We do not currently have a passenger rail, when we had it for a hundred years until the late 1960s. If I could get on a train that took me to Charleston, I would. If I could get on a train that took me to Columbia, I would. It matters to me because traffic is horrific and only getting worse.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Roads and Lost Productivity
body: I want us to tackle infrastructure because it isn't keeping up with population growth. It matters to me because it impacts every day life when you cannot access the services that you need.  I am very frustrated becaus I pay taxes but feel like I am not benefiting.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Infrastructure Can't Handle Growth
body: My top priority is infrastructure because the state isn't handling the population growth.  My grandchild is unable to attend the school closest to his house because there isn't room for him.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Generation Priced Out
body: South Carolina should focus on access to housing. With housing costs rising astronomically it is genuinely pricing an entire generation out of being able to start families, contribute to building their communities, and building wealth in the form of equity.  The middle class is disappearing. Housing is not supposed to be an inflationary asset and this is not the sign of a sustainable economy or asset. A large portion of South Carolinians live below the poverty line. Without a program to help restore housing in South Carolina, many native residents will be priced out of their birth state. The system does not work for us and we are desperately hoping for help.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Senior Struggles with Costs
body: My top priority is housing prices, which are crazy expensive here; even rentals are out of control. Salaries and hourly rates are so low. It's extremely difficult to own a home or find a rental that's not in the projects in North Charleston. Property and car insurance are so over priced. Even with the primary rate of 4%, it takes its toll. Taxes are too high. It matters to me because as a retired senior, it's very difficult to make ends meet month to month.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Need Roommates at 56
body: We should solve affordable housing. I'm considering getting roommates at 56 years old (not cool) just to survive.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Food and Housing Insecurity
body: We should solve food and housing insecurity. We live paycheck to paycheck, I have an adult child and a minor child that are disabled and they require more than most. I work at the hospital and my husband works in job recruitment. Not only are we feeling the impact, we are seeing it first hand. People can not get good jobs because jobs want 20 years of experience on relatively no income. People are so overwhelmed with taxes and medical bills and unable to get help that our low income programs are being utilized by so many people. After healthcare and taxes, I'm hardly bringing any income home.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Climate and Insurance Impact Housing
body: We should solve housing costs. It is one of the biggest challenges facing SC, however it is a result of multiple issues and not just the costs of building. Insurance rates continue to rise due to disasters related to changing climate. Energy costs are increasing and low wages, especially for minimum wage earners, make housing a major challenge. As a property owner, it affects me personally in increased costs to own a home. As a property manager, tenants struggle monthly with rising costs of utilities and rent payments.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Church Members Unhoused
body: I want us to tackle housing because many of my church members are unhoused.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Workforce Housing Crisis
body: My top priority is workforce housing because it is too expensive where tourism is popular. It means people have to travel long distances to get to their jobs in resorts, hotels, restaurants, bars, etc. We need affordable housing closer to where people work. If we can't have that, then we at least need better public transportation options. I see how it affects people in the coastal communities where workers live, supporting the more effluent areas.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Women's Choice Rights
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be banning abortions. It matters to me because not every woman should be able to make a choice.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Life-Saving Abortions Banned
body: I want us to tackle women's medical rights.  I've had to have three emergency medical abortions in the second trimester, all to save my life in wanted pregnancies. I would be dead if that happened now, so we can't try anymore if we live here.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Reproductive Healthcare Access
body: We should solve women's reproductive rights. I work in women's health and have friends who've needed services & medical care that is banned.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Premiums Jumped Dramatically
body: The one problem I'd solve is getting healthcare and preventative care to the population. My health plan costs are going up from $18.00/month to $200.00/month. There are many families here in SC that will not be able to afford this type of increase.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Insurance Costs Too High
body: I want to solve healthcare. The cost of my health insurance premiums will be 30% of my income.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Medicaid Expansion Needed
body: The one problem I'd solve is expanding Medicaid. It affects my household. My stepdaughter and grandson participate in it.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Wait Times and Misdiagnosis
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be healthcare reform. It matters to me because it's ridiculous that you have to wait for specialists appointments and then be misdiagnosed.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Rural Healthcare Access
body: My top priority is rural healthcare and lack of providers. I've been involved in the industry for 25 years and this keeps coming up as a major issue. People do not get the care that they need in rural areas.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Women's Healthcare Rights
body: I want us to improve women's rights for healthcare and equal pay.  Yes, because I'm a woman. All women deserve it.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Can't Afford Healthcare
body: We should solve healthcare. It matters to me because I can't pay the insurance fees on a fixed income.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: More Freedoms
body: I think the state government isn't the problem. I think the people need more education to understand the issues. We need more freedoms.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Need More Elections
body: I think there should be more elections. We need more turnover of our representatives including getting younger people into office.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Taxation Without Representation
body: South Carolina government needs to represent all the people not just a handful of like-minded donors. I live here. I am tired of taxation with no representation.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: 40% Have No Voice
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be 40% of the people have no voice. I am not heard or seen by lawmakers.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Single Party Rule Problem
body: I want us to change single party rule at the statehouse that supported partisan gerrymandering. My statehouse representative used to be a middle of the road representative whom I trusted to prioritize the needs of his constituency. Now I have a representative who receives a lot of outside funding and pushes policies that I don't support. This sounds like a political rant but it really is a desire for excellence rather than an acceptance of mediocrity through the lack of competing ideas and need to build consensus.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Political Ignorance is Depressing
body: I want us to fix partisan politics. It matters to me because there is an incredible ignorance of truth in politics and it is depressing and not getting us anywhere.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Gerrymandering Limits Representation
body: I want us to stop gerrymandering. It matters to me because makes it harder to elect people that align with my priorities. I don't feel represented.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Toxic Chemical Exposure
body: I want us to tackle toxic and hormone-disrupting chemicals and heavy metals, both old and newly applied, throughout our environment. Helicopters and road crews are spraying herbicides that are known toxins. As a biologist working on spills and a cancer survivor, I see this is a big risk to our state. The cancer rates and other health impacts in this state are very high.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Farmland Being Developed
body: I want us to tackle rapid, uncontrolled development. It matters to me because developers buying up all the farmlands around us.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Solar Farms Forced on Citizens
body: I want us to tackle mega solar farms that are being forced on local citizens who are not aware that is happening until it is too late. It has happened in my area.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Coastal Overgrowth
body: We should solve overgrowth on the coast because it is significant in our way of life and something that we are losing over time. It matters to me because it affects everyone with less beach access, costly beach access, and rising insurance costs due to flooding and other natural disasters.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Energy Costs Impact All
body: The one problem I'd solve is greater energy sufficiency. It matters to me because energy costs impact us all.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Climate Change Impact
body: South Carolina should focus on climate change. My family owns land on the sea islands in the Low Country. We are being pounded by intense storms, sea level rise, salt water intrusion etc.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Energy and Water Limits
body: We should solve in my area it is population growth. Our water and energy sources are being pushed to the limit. We now have peak hours of use where our energy rates increase drastically. Right now the blackout hours are 6am-9am.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Overbuilding Damages Environment
body: My top priority is over building. It matters to me because it wrecks the environment and displaces animals. There are too many stresses on the land.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Environmental Destruction
body: I want us to tackle protecting our environment. Just watch 1700 acres destroyed for an industry three blocks away from my house.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Farmer Water Concerns
body: The one problem I'd solve is water use management. I am a new regenerative grazing farmer. High quality water is a keystone of our survival.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Growth Without Planning
body: The one challenge I'd solve is unfettered growth without attention to infrastructure planning. Commute times, car accidents, and crime are increasing. I have been a victim of all.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Rapid Growth Strain
body: One of the biggest challenges South Carolina is facing right now is how fast the state is growing and how hard it is for our infrastructure, housing, and services to keep up. Roads are crowded, housing costs are rising, and many communities still struggle with access to good healthcare and education. People love living here, but the rapid growth is exposing gaps that really need attention so the state can stay healthy, safe, and sustainable for everyone. Yes, this affects me personally because the gaps show up every day. I experienced firsthand how the low pay and constant strain of the education system lead to burnout, which ultimately pushed me to step away from a field I cared deeply about.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Water Quality Crisis
body: One of the biggest challenges in South Carolina right now is the quality of water. I believe it is more than just old infrastructure. The water plant operations should be tested to figure out how to improve the actual water for residents. This situation affects me personally, as well as many other residents in Florence county. We constantly have to boil water. We spend lots of money on bottled water to cook and drink.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Preserve SC Identity
body: South Carolina has a lot people moving into our state. How do we keep this from changing the identity of our state? I love SC and I don't want it to change to be like other states. I want newcomers to be a part of us, not come change things.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Ignoring Black History
body: South Carolina should focus on the fact that it still continues to whitewash and erase history of the African and African Americans who built this state. It affects everyone as we all remain uneducated and miseducated.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Women in Leadership
body: We need more women in leadership roles across the state. In elected office, in business, and everywhere else. Women are not fairly represented in decision-making and they are over 50% of the population.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Mutual Respect in Legislature
body: My top priority is mutual respect among legislators. It is ok to disagree, but be respectful.  Have lunch together after a difficult but respectful debate. It matters to me because it impacts the whole population and how we see our identity in South Carolina. They are the leaders of our state and should set a better example for the wider society.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Elderly and Disabled Care
body: My top priority is decent care for the elderly and disabled. I am 60 years old and with 2 strokes unable to walk or talk. My husband is 46 blind and on dialysis and is recovering from triple bypass surgery.  It is very hard for us.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Book Bans in Schools
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be the erosions of our freedoms. Books are banned from the libraries in my kids' school district.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: LGBT Discrimination
body: If we could fix one problem, it would be partisan politics. The partisan politics has been discriminating and scapegoating against LGBT people for years and I'm LGBT.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Rights Being Taken Away
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be partisan politics. It matters to me because they are taking away our rights.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Lost Ability to Unite
body: We have seem to lost the ability to unite towards a collective future that represents the broad spectrum of ideas and objectives. Being divisive only hurts us. It keeps our eyes on our own feet. It matters to me because discourse has declined and we are lacking meaningful conversation that allows for forward movement.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Race Relations and Equality
body: The one problem I'd solve is race relations and the lack of opportunity and equality. It matters to me because everyone deserves the chance to succeed.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Losing SC Identity
body: The one problem I'd solve is loosing our South Carolina identity. Losing agriculture is huge and as it's the state's backbone. Losing land to development is ccreating a loss for local residents.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Rural Roads Dangerous
body: I want to fix the roads especially the secondary ones. We live in a semi rural area and the roads are too narrow and pot hole filled. This leads to reoccuring tire and wheel damage and it makes for dangerous driving situations.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Unequal Road Maintenance
body: My top priority is road and bridge paving and repair.  It needs to be spread equally across the state in a more efficient manner. The roads then need to be maintained properly to extend their useful life span--and not concentrated in areas of powerful politicians. Bad roads cause excessive wear and tear on my vehicles. It results in increased maintenance and shorter life span creating added expenses.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Dangerous Drivers Everywhere
body: My biggest concern is people driving like maniacs. They are running lights, speeding, and driving too close. I absolutely hate leaving my house any more than necessary. I've witnessed so many accidents or near accidents, including accidents leading to deaths. I've personally been involved in so many near accidents due to poor drivers.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Cyclist Safety Issues
body: My top priority is infrastructure: oads, bike paths, public transit, clean water, renewable energy. It is not keeping pace with our state's growth. As an avid cyclist and walker, I experience the deficiencies in safe roads several times a week.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Can't Get Point A to B
body: My top priority is crappy infrastructure. It matters to me because can't get from point a to point b without excessive traffic and poorly maintained roads.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Potholes Safety Concern
body: I want us to tackle poorly maintained roads. It matters to me because pot holes and poorly drained roads are a safety concern.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Vehicle Repair Costs
body: I want us to improve our roads. It matters to me because I spend countless dollars on vehicle repair because of how\ bad the roads are.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Widen 95 and 26
body: I want us to widen 95 and 26. It matters to me because travel through the state is so dangerous. At this point, traveling on holidays is impossible and it keeps families apart.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Poor Driving Skills
body: I want us to improve road safety and the lack of driving skills. It matters to me because every drive is a risk because people do not know what is correct.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Culture Wars Distract from Real Issues
body: I want us to address the partisan politics created by our government that is focused on culture war issues instead of real issues facing our state. Our infrastructure is crumbling. Our schools are underfunded. These are important issues that need to be fixed for the future of our state.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Partisanship Attacks Rights
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be partisanship controlling the state government. It matters to me because yes, attacks on individual rights, free speech and public education.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Tax Accountability Lacking
body: My top priority is extreme taxes. There is no accountability or transparency in this state.  South Carolina residents pay multiple forms of taxation, including on food, clothing, vehicles, property, and income. Despite this significant tax burden, the condition of our roads remains poor, and the public education system continues to face serious challenges. Greater transparency, accountability, and strategic investment are needed to ensure taxpayer dollars are producing measurable improvements in infrastructure and education.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Corruption Undermines Trust
body: South Carolina should focus on corruption. It matters to me because corruption at the state level undermines our community and collective trust in systems. If everyone is apathetic to the corruption of the legislature then no one will ever take action to stop it.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Better Elderly and Disabled Care
body: I want us to tackle a lack of compassion, accountability, and accomodations for the elderly and disabled. I am a sole caregiver for two relatives and I struggle with the frustration from this all the time.  I need more help and support to care for my family members.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Political Division Hurts Relationships
body: We should solve cultural disharmony.  There is growing distrust and hate between races, genders, political parties, etc. It has pulled apart family and friends whilst also causing me to be less friendly and open-minded. I'm a right-leaning moderate ("independent") male. People from both sides of the aisle don't like my views.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Poor Leadership Decisions
body: My top priority is unsuitable leadership. It matters to me because it is frustrating to see bad decisions being made. I am very weary of their decision making that results in more hardships for residents.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Gerrymandering and Representation
body: We need to stop gerrymandering, which has led to super majorities in the statehouse. It matters to me because there is a lack of representation in state policy making.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Family Court Corruption
body: If we could address one problem, it would be lack of resources and family court corruption. I cannot afford or get legal help to stop violation of a court order and the harmthat is being done to me.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Need More Diverse Leadership
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be lack of diversified leadership. It matters to me because making decisions and passing laws without including the opposite sex or minority input is wrong and prejudiced.  We need more diversity in our elected office.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Broken Judicial Ethics
body: I want us to tackle the broken judicial system. It matters to me because it affects the ethics for the entire state.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Career Politicians Problem
body: I want us to fix lack of true leadership because career politicians do not have the citizens best interests in mind. I want a government that speaks up for the people and actually helps them with their issues.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Legislature Ignores Voters
body: I want us to tackle the difference between what the polls show South Carolinians care about and what our legislature spends their time on.  It affects everyone in South Carolina who would like to see our leaders be responsive to all their voters, not just the 10% of their base who helped them win their primaries.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Children and Gun Violence
body: South Carolina should focus on reducing violence and gun violence. I'm tired and sad of reading about so many children being shot.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Murder of Family Member
body: My top priority is crime. It matters to me because my family member was murdered.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Poverty Overwhelms Courts
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be poverty. I work in the law. So many poor people are unrepresented it overwhelms the courts.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Harm Reduction Programs Needed
body: South Carolina should focus on Low Country harm reduction programs to help educate the community and those with active substance use disorder. I work with this under represented group of South Carolinians daily and I see the importance of this service.  It is disheartening to see people who want change but are not be supported by the community.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Mass Incarceration Crisis
body: My top priority is mass incarceration. Many of my peers, family and friends are sitting behind bars because of over sentenced by the judicial system.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Farm and Family Survival
body: South Carolina should focus on input prices and commodity markets. It matters to me because it is difficult to save a family and a farm.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Meeting Basic Needs
body: We need to care of all our people. It doesn't affect me personally I have a close family but it hurts to see people not having their basic needs met.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Division and Food Bank Shame
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be extreme division fueled by economic disparities. I've gone to some food banks. My kids have been bullied because of it.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Keeping Young Talent Here
body: The biggest problem the state faces is keeping the younger intellectual generation here. There isn't enough industry--and look at the colleges.  There is major disparity. I want every South Carolinian to be treated with dignity and have equal opportunities.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Need for Education Innovation
body: The one problem I'd solve is innovation in the public school system. Learn a lesson from Mississippi, who found new ways to improve education. I know because I am an educator.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Public School Quality Crisis
body: My top priority is SC is in the lower third of every national ranking of k-12 public education metrics. The partisan politics answer is to give up and give stipends for school "choice". This eventually further erodes public school quality and, ultimately, corrodes the societal and cultural fabric of our communities. I have 4 grandsons in public school and I want the best education possible for them. The real challenge is keeping our state competitive and prosperous while also being a safe and nurturing place for all citizens.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Education Lifts from Poverty
body: I want us to tackle education. Education is essential to lifting South Carolinians out of poverty. Education is essential to a healthy population as well. Yes, when our population doesn't know how to read and write, when our population is ignorant on making healthy lifestyle choices, it affects all of us.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Education Reform
body: We need stronger education reform: restructuring schools to create graduate students who are truly work-ready. Strengthening technical colleges: expanding and enhancing programs to supply skilled workers for industry. It matters to me because we need a better future.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Schools Drive Community Growth
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be education. The education system in our area is crucial for community growth. Our community's development is contingent upon the improvement of our schools. Unless our education system is enhanced, it is unlikely that individuals will stay here, and consequently, industries and companies will not establish themselves in the area.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Support for Teachers Needed
body: South Carolina should focus on lack of support for teachers and public education. I have children and I worry about their future and the low quality of education.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Poor Education Impacts All
body: I want us to tackle weak education. It matters to me because a poorly educated state impacts everyone and their future.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Education Ranking Decline
body: One of the biggest challenges South Carolina faces is the continual decline of our education and the continued low ranking compared to other states in the nation. I am a public school teacher in South Carolina and a product of South Carolina public schools. Beyond my direct involvement, education impacts me and every other South Carolinian in one way or another.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Teacher Development Matters
body: My top priority is pre k-12 teacher development and retention. I have a 7-month old great granddaughter whose mother is an educator, as is her father, as was his father. She deserves the best education.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Teacher Recruitment and Retention
body: We should solve how this state recruits and keeps quality teachers. It matters to me because we need dedicated teachers at the front of the classroom.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Quality Education Investment
body: The one problem I'd solve is quality education at all levels. Education generates tomorrow's citizen. The next generation are the citizens that create the future of our state and America.  They deserve better education.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: School-to-Prison Pipeline
body: I want us to tackle prison reform, especially the school to prison pipeline needs to be dismantled. As a result of it so many are being misdiagnosed, therefore, leaving them with a psychotic drug dependency. As a controlling mechanism they go from home to school to jail. For 20 yrs I have been fighting for change beginning with my son.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Economic Inequality Gap
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be economic parity between the people who have more and the working poor.  It is very unfair and I see my fellow neighbors struggling.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Can't Save for College
body: I am discouraged by the fact that I cannot save enough money for college. The cost of living is too high and I work two jobs.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Can't Afford the Basics
body: I am unable to make enough money to pay for my famliy's basic needs. I went to college and I've worked for 20 years. Why can't I afford the basics?!
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Children's Future Affordability
body: We should solve affordability. It directly affects my children's' ability to make an independent life for themselves and their future families.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Healthcare Worker Undervalued
body: One of the biggest challenges facing South Carolina right now is the combination of low wages, limited worker benefits, and widespread economic insecurity, which interacts with problems in education, housing, and healthcare to make it harder for many residents to get ahead. I am a certified medical assistant by trade. I have worked in the industry for nearly 30 years. I have been unemployed for 11 months now since moving here because I will not take a job paying $15/per hour for my skill set.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Lack of Economic Investment
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be no economic prosperity because there is no major investment. It matters to me because there's a major lack of jobs in the states. No investment = poverty.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: State Minimum Wage Crisis
body: The one problem I'd solve is too low state minimum wage, which is stuck at $7 dollars an hour. It matters to me because it is hard to get a good paying job.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Fixed Income Grocery Costs
body: My top priority is cost of living because it has gotten so high. Groceries usually run me over $100 each week. I am 71 and live on a fixed income.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Manufacturing Wages Too Low
body: South Carolina should focus on decent manufacturing jobs and wages that will support a family. My co-workers and I make $12 an hour. It is barely enough to live on.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Feeding Family Costs
body: South Carolina should focus on cost of living. It matters to me because it affects daily life and my ability to feed my family.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Need for Well-Paying Jobs
body: The one problem I'd solve is jobs. It matters to me because we need well paying ones to survive.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Youth Employment Struggles
body: We need good paying jobs. I'm retired but I see so many young people struggling.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: High-Paying Tech Jobs
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be we need more high paying white collar jobs in information technology. Yes, I would like to remain in SC and not have to relocate to Virginia.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Low Wages and Union Support
body: I want us to tackle low wages and the lack of unions to protect workers. It matters to me workers don't have leverage over their employers.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Rising Cost of Living
body: South Carolina should focus on price inflation of food, services and energy. Cost of living has dramatically increased causing me to cut back.  It is harder to afford my basic needs.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Division Blocks Progress
body: We should tackle the divided political structure. It affects most people including me because we can't get anything accomplished.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Overcrowding Stress
body: My top priority is infrastructure. Overcrowding. It gets my stress level up with all the cars and nowhere to go. People are running red lights and turning left and cutting people off. Government only cares about the money and doesn't care about us.
project_title: Welcome to The South Carolina Forum!

title: Economic Opportunity for All
body: If we could solve one problem, it would be economic opportunity for all residents. It matters to me because the lack of opportunity leads to poor outcomes, like higher crime, more reliance on government subsidies, and a lower quality of life for everyone.

project_title: The South Carolina Forum: Pre-Launch Survey
custom_field_values.what_makes_south_car: Carolina is my chosen state.  I was born and raised in Ann Arbor, MI with all the rich resources that living in a University town brings. My choosing SC as my "forever" home is based on exposure to options, not generational allegiance.  People are good here, well, at least until the past perhaps 10 years, when social media has fueled the Red/Blue hatred wars.  I have lost friends, alas.
custom_field_values.what_would_you_tell_: Yes. I am 83 years old, with an MBA.  I live on Social Security and a small bit of funds from the sale of my home 5 years ago.  I live in a rural county seat, although the town is much more prosperous than the rest of the county.
custom_field_values.are_there_other_chal: I am very concerned about young people.  AI, social media,  and other youth problems have made me think that we, as a state, as a nation, are losing the educated and socially competent people that we need to assume leadership in the near future.  We cannot continue to be led by the "elders".
custom_field_values.what_problems_do_you: health care for people who are barely above the Federal poverty line, but so poor that they cannot afford insurance.  A corollary to this problem is the rural population and the elderly on fixed incomes.

project_title: The South Carolina Forum: Pre-Launch Survey
custom_field_values.what_makes_south_car: My husband and I grew up in Columbia, went to a state college, left SC  for 15 years, and came back to take care of aging parents and raise our children who are now almost grown. I hate that the politics in our state make us consider leaving again.
custom_field_values.what_would_you_tell_:
My kids are almost finished (college sophomore and high school
junior), but both ended up going to the S.C. Governor’s School for the Arts, partially because they have a passion for the arts, but also because their zoned school was not meeting their needs. As a daughter and sister of career public school teachers in S.C. (and a grad of S.C. public schools), I see how the public schools have been decreasing in quality/success because of so many factors, and the future of our state depends on fixing this problem for ALL students/schools. This will take money, not only paying teachers more, but decreasing class sizes, more social workers, psychologists, parent educators, etc.
custom_field_values.are_there_other_chal: I think the public school issues both affect and are affected by the issue of gun violence, especially young people (both homocides and suicides). custom_field_values.what_problems_do_you: Failing public education, not only in low income areas, all public schools! Our future (economics, safety, health, welfare, criminal system, etc) all depend on quality public education. This includes parent ed, so that parents do their part to provide a safe, supportive home life that allows students and teachers to succeed at school.

project_title: The South Carolina Forum: Pre-Launch Survey
custom_field_values.what_makes_south_car: South Carolina feels special to me because it has this blend of history, beauty, and community that you cannot find anywhere else. Living in Charleston especially, I love the sense of place, the energy of the city, and the kindness of the people who make it feel like home. There is something about the culture, the coastal landscape, and the way neighbors look out for each other that makes this state meaningful to me in a really personal way.  I like being a part of the solution and making a better South Carolina for our future!
custom_field_values.what_would_you_tell_: Yes, this affects me personally because navigating healthcare in South Carolina can feel really challenging, especially when it comes to finding timely care and specialists. The gaps in access and the strain on the system show up in everyday life, and it becomes even harder for people dealing with chronic health issues, women’s health concerns, or anyone who needs consistent medical support. Also, as a former educator, I experienced firsthand how the low pay and constant strain of the education system lead to burnout, which ultimately pushed me to step away from a field I cared deeply about.
custom_field_values.are_there_other_chal: I am also thinking a lot about the bigger picture challenges in South Carolina, like the need for stronger infrastructure that can actually keep up with how fast the state is growing, and the ongoing struggle to pass common sense gun laws that keep communities safe. Protecting womens reproductive rights is another major issue, because access to care should not depend on politics. I also believe we would benefit from term limits to bring in fresh leadership and reduce entrenched power. And honestly, we need a return to real civil discourse where people can disagree without attacking each other, so we can actually solve problems instead of getting stuck in constant conflict.
custom_field_values.what_problems_do_you: One of the biggest challenges South Carolina is facing right now is how fast the state is growing and how hard it is for our infrastructure, housing, and services to keep up. Roads are crowded, housing costs are rising, and many communities still struggle with access to good healthcare and education. People love living here, but the rapid growth is exposing gaps that really need attention so the state can stay healthy, safe, and sustainable for everyone.

Yes. At the national level (presidential & congressional elections) as an "independent" in a Ruby Red state my voice and my issues aren't addressed. 
Deployment and misuse of the USNG is a prime example.  As a veteran with over 30 years of active duty service, watching our Governor play politics and misusing the SCNG betrays the trust the US military built with the American people post Vietnam and the tragic events at Kent State University in 1970. Electoral reform. "Politics is the allocation of resources." We can't even write in a vote for President. The political parties of SC dictate who we vote for, not the people.
We need to move to Ranked Choice Voting
End Gerrymandered districts
Make sure we have truly open (nonpartisan) primaries
lower the barriers to getting on the ballot
reign in dark money in politics.
Thomas Jefferson is quoted as saying, "We in America do not have government by the majority--we have government by the majority who participate . . . All tyranny needs to gain a foothold is for the people of good conscience to remain silent."

Our political system silences people of good conscience.

project_title: The South Carolina Forum: Pre-Launch Survey
custom_field_values.what_makes_south_car: There are too many things to list that makes South Carolina special to me.
custom_field_values.what_would_you_tell_:
I do not personally have Medicaid however, there are thousands of community members that do. 

A large number of South Carolinians exceed the income limit to be eligible for Medicaid, but also don’t make enough to afford care from the health insurance marketplace, leaving them with no healthcare options in between.
This is called the Coverage Gap.

In 1965 the US passed Medicare insurance for seniors and Medicaid insurance for low income people of any age. In Medicaid, states have the flexibility to set eligibility for different groups. Most states set relatively high income eligibility for children and pregnant women.  

However, because there was no overall national standard for Medicaid eligibility and employers were increasingly dropping insurance for their workforce, growing numbers of working age adults became uninsured. 

To solve that problem, in 2010 the US passed the Affordable Care Act which mandated coverage for all low income working age (19 – 64) adults under the same income eligibility at 138% of poverty. However, a Supreme Court decision allows this expanded coverage to be at State discretion. To date, 40 states have extended coverage under the Affordable Care Act – SC is one of only 10 states that have not, leaving a large health insurance coverage gap for thousands of people.

Over 340,000 residents of South Carolina would receive affordable healthcare if the coverage gap were closed today
custom_field_values.are_there_other_chal: Transportation options for people with disabilities is extremely limited. Even in the larger cities like Columbia and Greenville, there are not enough pair of transit vehicles or drivers to keep up with the demand.

I work hard and am a single mother, full time employee, and graduate student, and I would do anything for my kids, but we need a system that make it EASIER to raise children in a healthy, safer society.
custom_field_values.are_there_other_chal:
We must protect workers’ rights instead of the corporation’s rights! Raise minimum wage, expand unions, and provide free universal healthcare. Also on my mind: public safety (too many shootings; need gun reform), cost of living (soooo high); free and expanded public transit; walkable/bikeable communities; renewable energy; building energy codes MUST be updated to at least IECC 2015 codes; we should be transitioning freight, medium sized delivery, fleets, and personal vehicles to EVs; we need expanded EV charging infrastructure and we need our roads to be repaired. Natural lands should be protected. We should zone land on the coast and in floodplains as no-build areas (sea level rise and extreme weather events are increasing flooding); we need to focus on our low-income communities and provide subsidies on home weatherization retrofits.

The attack on women’s rights. House bill 323 was terrifying; so far right that even the GOP couldn’t back it. It’s been proposed at least twice now and I imagine will come back up again in the future. It is a threat to women, doctors, supportive family members, and will result in death if passed. We need access to abortion. We need to change the current law to allow abortion longer than 6 weeks. 

We also need to support our families with universal free childcare and preschool, more funding for our public education system, no banned books, and teachers must be paid more. Children are our future and EVERY child should have the right to quality, free education.
